pharm: Type II 5alpha-reductase inhibitor; blocks conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT)
quick: Contraindicated; do not handle tablets if pregnant
summary: Finasteride is a Type II 5alpha-reductase inhibitor that lowers dihydrotestosterone (DHT). At 1 mg once daily it is indicated for male pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) in men only and is not indicated for use in women or children. It is Pregnancy Category X: women who are or may be pregnant must not handle crushed or broken tablets because of the risk of abnormal external genitalia in a male fetus. Daily use for three or more months is generally needed before benefit is seen, and finasteride lowers serum PSA by roughly 50% (must be considered when interpreting PSA).
indications: Treatment of male pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) in MEN ONLY
Not indicated for use in women
Not indicated for use in pediatric patients
Efficacy in bitemporal recession has not been established

dosage.n: Daily use for three months or more is generally necessary before benefit is observed; continued use needed to sustain benefit
Benefit should be re-evaluated periodically; withdrawal of treatment leads to reversal of effect within 12 months
No dosage adjustment necessary in renal impairment
No dosage adjustment necessary based on pharmacokinetics; efficacy in elderly not established

dosage.n: 5 mg formulation (BPH) is dosed at five times the hair-loss strength; this label is for the 1 mg product

Tablets are film-coated to prevent contact with the active ingredient during normal handling
Women who are or may become pregnant must not handle crushed or broken tablets

Re-evaluate benefit periodically; effect reverses within 12 months of stopping
moa: Finasteride is a competitive and specific inhibitor of Type II 5alpha-reductase, an intracellular enzyme that converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT). Inhibition blocks the peripheral conversion of testosterone to DHT, producing significant decreases in serum and scalp tissue DHT. In men with androgenetic alopecia the balding scalp contains miniaturized follicles and increased DHT; lowering DHT interrupts a key factor in the development of hair loss. Finasteride has no affinity for the androgen receptor.

absolute: Pregnancy - contraindicated in women who are or may potentially be pregnant (risk to male fetus)
Hypersensitivity to any component of the product
relative: Women in general (not indicated for use in women)
Liver function abnormalities (caution; extensive hepatic metabolism)
monitor: Serum PSA - finasteride decreases PSA and a confirmed rise may signal prostate cancer

preg: Pregnancy Category X. Contraindicated in women who are or may become pregnant. As a Type II 5alpha-reductase inhibitor finasteride prevents conversion of testosterone to DHT, a hormone necessary for normal development of male external genitalia; in animal studies it caused abnormal external genital development (including hypospadias) in male fetuses. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant must not handle crushed or broken tablets because of possible absorption and risk to a male fetus; intact coated tablets prevent contact during normal handling. If a pregnant woman contacts crushed or broken tablets, wash the area immediately with soap and water. Exposure through the semen of a treated male partner is considered very low (semen levels are minute and far below doses affecting DHT).
lact: Finasteride is not indicated for use in women. It is not known whether finasteride is excreted in human milk.
renal: No dosage adjustment is necessary in patients with renal impairment. In chronic renal impairment (CrCl 9 to 55 mL/min) AUC, peak concentration, half-life, and protein binding after a single dose were similar to healthy volunteers; urinary excretion of metabolites was decreased with a compensatory increase in fecal excretion.
hepatic: The effect of hepatic impairment on finasteride pharmacokinetics has not been studied. Because finasteride is extensively metabolized in the liver, caution should be used when administering it to patients with liver function abnormalities.

minor: No drug interactions of clinical importance have been identified
Does not appear to affect the cytochrome P450-linked drug-metabolizing enzyme system; no clinically meaningful interaction with antipyrine, digoxin, propranolol, theophylline, or warfarin
interactions.food: Bioavailability is not affected by food; may be taken with or without meals.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction with alcohol is described in the label.
interactions.diagnostics: Decreases serum PSA by approximately 50% in older men with BPH and lowers PSA in younger men; account for this when interpreting PSA. May cause PSA decreases even in the presence of prostate cancer. A confirmed rise from the lowest on-treatment PSA value should be evaluated.

serious: Possible increased risk of high-grade (Gleason 8-10) prostate cancer with 5alpha-reductase inhibitors
rare: Persistent sexual dysfunction after discontinuation (reported post-marketing)
emergency: Severe allergic reaction (e.g., angioedema, swelling of lips/face/throat, difficulty breathing)

monitoring: Serum PSA before and during therapy; interpret with awareness of ~50% reduction
Evaluate any confirmed PSA increase from the lowest on-treatment value
Sexual adverse effects (libido, erectile and ejaculatory function)
Continued need for and benefit of therapy, re-evaluated periodically
counsel: This medicine is for men only; women who are or may be pregnant must not handle crushed or broken tablets
If a pregnant woman contacts a crushed or broken tablet, wash the area immediately with soap and water
Take one 1 mg tablet once daily, with or without food
It may take three months or more of daily use before you see benefit, and benefit reverses within 12 months of stopping
Tell your doctor about decreased sex drive, erection problems, ejaculation changes, breast lumps/tenderness, or mood/depression
Inform any doctor checking your prostate that you take finasteride, since it lowers PSA
pk: DHT suppression reaches ~65% within 24 hours; clinical hair benefit after >=3 months
Peak plasma concentration 1 to 2 hours after a 1 mg dose
~4.5 to 6 hours in men 18-60 years; ~8 hours in men over 70
Once-daily dosing; slow enzyme turnover prolongs DHT suppression
Store at 20-25C (68-77F); keep container closed and protect from moisture
pearls: Two strengths exist: 1 mg for androgenetic alopecia (men) and 5 mg for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)
Lowers serum PSA by roughly 50% - double the measured value when screening for prostate cancer
Pregnancy Category X - women who are or may be pregnant must never handle crushed or broken tablets (hypospadias / abnormal male genitalia)
Bioavailability is unaffected by food; extensively metabolized by CYP3A4 but clinically important drug interactions are not identified
Effect reverses within 12 months of discontinuation; intact tablets are coated to prevent skin contact
5alpha-reductase inhibitors may increase the risk of high-grade prostate cancer
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember the same day. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular once-daily schedule. Do not take two tablets to make up for a missed dose. Consistent daily use over months is needed for benefit.
overdose: Single doses up to 400 mg and multiple doses up to 80 mg/day for three months did not produce adverse reactions in clinical studies. No specific antidote or treatment for finasteride overdose can be recommended; manage supportively. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222) for guidance.
